title: Nabaa evaluation question set
description: The shape run_eval.py consumes. Deliberately contains no questions: a system evaluated against questions its own author chose is measuring the author. Only id, question and answerable are required; every other field is scored when present and skipped when absent, so a partially specified set still yields the metrics it can support rather than failing or being guessed at.

corpus.description: Which documents the set was written against, recorded in every result file so a comparison across a corpus change is not mistaken for a comparison across a code change.

author.description: Who wrote the set. Recorded because independence is the point.

id.description: Stable across runs, so before/after lines up question by question.

question.description: Exactly as it would be typed into the Chat screen.

answerable.description: false means the documents genuinely do not contain the answer. Those questions score refusal accuracy; answering one is the worst outcome the harness measures.

expected_document.description: Filename as uploaded. Scored with expected_pages.

expected_pages.description: Any overlap with the cited page range counts, because a passage spanning a page boundary is not wrong.

expected_clause.description: Clause number only, e.g. "A.1" or "8.2". A citation to a subclause of the expected clause counts: "10.2" is satisfied by "10.2.3", because that is right rather than nearly right.

expected_answer_contains.description: Substrings that must appear in the returned passage text - typically the figure and its unit. Case-insensitive. ALL must be present, so a question asking for two values is only correct when both come back.

note.description: Free text for the set's author. Never scored.
